title: Automated_negotiation
summary:
Automated negotiation is a form of interaction in systems composed of multiple autonomous agents, in which the aim is to reach agreements through an iterative process of making offers. It is defined as the process by which a group of actors communicate with one another aiming to reach a mutually acceptable agreement on some matter, where at least one of the actors is an autonomous software agent.

Automated negotiation systems can offer solutions to challenges in manual negotiation through their round-the-clock availability, the ability to negotiate without emotional bias, efficient information access, and seamless integration of cultural contexts. The trend of automated negotiation replacing manual negotiation is gradually becoming apparent; for example, Walmart has employed Pactum AI to negotiate with suppliers, saving an average of 3% annually in rebates, while 75% of suppliers prefer negotiating with the AI over humans.

Related areas include content negotiation, in which user agents negotiate over HTTP about how to best represent a web resource, and negotiation support systems, in which negotiation decision-making activities are supported by an information system.
